description: Comprehensive chart, diagram, and visualization specifications based on McKinsey, BCG, and Bain best practices. Designed for executive-level business documents and presentations.

designPrinciples.clarity: Every visualization should answer 'So what?' within 3 seconds
designPrinciples.simplicity: Remove all non-essential elements (Tufte's data-ink ratio)
designPrinciples.actionability: Visualizations should drive decisions, not just display data
designPrinciples.consistency: Use consistent colors, fonts, and styles across all visuals
designPrinciples.accessibility: Ensure color-blind friendly palettes and clear labels

primary.name: Omega Professional
primary.description: Primary brand colors for Omega documents

sequential.name: Blue Sequential (5-step)
sequential.description: For progressive data (low to high values)
sequential.usage: Heat maps, choropleth maps, graduated data

diverging.name: Red-Blue Diverging
diverging.description: For data with positive/negative or opposing values
diverging.usage: Variance analysis, sentiment analysis, performance gaps

categorical.name: Big 3 Standard (6 categories)
categorical.usage: Bar charts, pie charts, categorical comparisons
categorical.note: Beyond 6 categories, use grouped/stacked charts or filter data

trafficLight.name: Traffic Light (RAG Status)
trafficLight.usage: KPI dashboards, risk matrices, project status

specifications.colors: Use categorical palette or single color with gradient
specifications.baseline: Always start Y-axis at zero for bar charts

specifications.colors: Highlight top 3 or key insight in accent color
specifications.sorting: Descending order by value (unless natural order exists)

specifications.markers: Use for <20 data points, hide for >20
specifications.colors: Primary series in brand color, others in muted tones
specifications.legend: Top-right or bottom, sorted by final value

waterfall.name: Waterfall Chart
exampleUseCases: Customer churn analysis (start → additions → losses → end)

pie.name: Pie Chart

specifications.colors: Categorical palette or gradient from dark to light
specifications.alternative: Use bar chart for >6 categories or similar values

pie.mcKinseyRule: Pie charts are rarely the best choice. Consider bar chart first.

donut.name: Donut Chart
bestFor: Same as pie, with center metric (total, average)

specifications.centerMetric: Display total or key insight in center

scatter.name: Scatter Plot
bestFor: Portfolio analysis (2x2 matrix with continuous axes)

specifications.markerSize: Based on third dimension (bubble chart) or uniform
specifications.colors: By category or gradient by value
specifications.dataLabels: For outliers or top N points only

exampleUseCases: BCG Growth-Share Matrix (growth rate vs market share)

specifications.colors: Bars in brand color, line in contrasting color
specifications.legend: Clearly label which metric uses which axis

specifications.colors: Darkest at bottom, lightest at top
specifications.baseline: Bottom layer should be most important or stable

heatmap.name: Heat Map
bestFor: Matrix of values with color intensity

specifications.cellLabels: Show actual values for small matrices (<10x10)
specifications.legend: Show color scale with min/max values

exampleUseCases: Website activity by hour × day of week

matrix2x2.name: 2x2 Matrix
matrix2x2.description: Classic consulting framework for categorizing items across two dimensions

dataPoints.sizing: By third dimension (e.g., revenue, market size)
dataPoints.labeling: Top N or all if <10 points

examples: BCG Growth-Share Matrix (Market Growth Rate vs Relative Market Share)
GE-McKinsey Matrix (Industry Attractiveness vs Competitive Strength)
designNotes: Reference lines at midpoints to create quadrants
Annotate each quadrant with strategic implications
Use bubble size for third dimension
Label axes clearly with low/high indicators

pyramid.name: Pyramid Diagram
pyramid.description: Hierarchical representation showing levels from broad base to narrow top

structure.colors: Gradient from dark (bottom/top) to light, or categorical by level
structure.labels: Inside each level with percentage or count

funnel.name: Funnel Chart
funnel.description: Shows progressive reduction through stages of a process

structure.widthCalculation: Proportional to volume at each stage
structure.colors: Single color with decreasing opacity or gradient
structure.dataLabels: Volume and % of original at each stage

processFlow.name: Process Flow Diagram
processFlow.description: Sequential steps with decision points and feedback loops
bestPractices: Group related steps with background shading

orgChart.name: Organization Chart
orgChart.description: Hierarchical structure of roles and reporting relationships

structure.connectors: Vertical and horizontal lines showing reporting

designNotes: Compact layout to fit on one page/slide

timeline.name: Timeline / Gantt Chart
timeline.description: Project schedule showing tasks, durations, and dependencies

bars.style: Solid for committed, striped for tentative

stakeholderMap.name: Stakeholder Map / Power-Interest Matrix
stakeholderMap.description: Categorizes stakeholders by influence and interest level

riskHeatMap.name: Risk Heat Map
riskHeatMap.description: Visual representation of risks by probability and impact

valueChain.name: Value Chain Diagram
valueChain.description: Porter's Value Chain showing primary and support activities

swimLane.name: Swimlane Diagram
swimLane.description: Process flow showing different actors/departments in horizontal lanes

structure.colors: By lane or by process type

iconLibrary.description: Standard icon set for consulting documents (recommended: Noun Project, Font Awesome, or custom)

specifications.colors: Solid fills in brand colors or monochrome
specifications.spacing: Consistent padding around icons in layouts

axisLabels.format: Abbreviate units (M for millions, % for percent)

dataLabels.precision: 0 decimals for large numbers, 1-2 for small/rates

annotations.usage: Call out key insights, explain anomalies

chartTitleFormulas.description: McKinsey-style chart titles that answer 'So what?' rather than just describe the data
goodExamples: Product A drives 60% of revenue, creating concentration risk
Customer satisfaction declined 15pts in Q3, primarily in region EMEA
Market share gains in premium segment offset losses in mass market

optional: Gridlines (very light, if needed for reading precision)

raster.resolution: 300 DPI minimum for print, 150 DPI for screen

colorBlindness: Avoid red-green combinations without additional indicators
Use patterns/textures in addition to colors
Provide text alternatives for color-coded information
contrast: Avoid light colors on light backgrounds
Use WCAG AA or AAA standards
textAlternatives: Include data table for complex charts
Ensure key insights are in text, not just visuals

chartingLibraries.name: Plotly
chartingLibraries.bestFor: Interactive dashboards, HTML reports, PoC tools

pythonDataVisualization.description: Python stack for Big 3-quality data analysis and visualization

coreLibraries.name: matplotlib
coreLibraries.usage: Excel-embedded charts, PDF reports, print materials

coreLibraries.name: Plotly
coreLibraries.usage: HTML dashboards, client PoC tools, web presentations

pythonDocumentGeneration.description: Python stack for professional document generation

excelGeneration.name: openpyxl
excelGeneration.purpose: Native Excel workbook creation and manipulation
excelGeneration.bestFor: Complex formatting, formulas, charts, conditional formatting
excelGeneration.omegaUsage: Banking-grade financial models, CAPEX analysis, risk registers

excelGeneration.name: xlsxwriter
excelGeneration.bestFor: Large datasets, performance-critical workbooks, chart generation

excelGeneration.name: pandas.ExcelWriter
excelGeneration.bestFor: Quick data export, multi-sheet workbooks from DataFrames
excelGeneration.omegaUsage: Data analysis exports, pivot table outputs

wordGeneration.name: python-docx
wordGeneration.purpose: Create Word documents from scratch programmatically
wordGeneration.bestFor: Data-heavy reports, automated document generation, simple layouts
wordGeneration.omegaUsage: Technical appendices, data tables, auto-generated sections

wordGeneration.name: docxtpl
wordGeneration.bestFor: High-stakes client reports where branding is critical, mail merge
wordGeneration.workflow: Designer creates .docx template → Python fills data placeholders

wordGeneration.name: Spire.Doc
wordGeneration.bestFor: Complex document merging, Word-to-PDF conversion, advanced formatting
wordGeneration.omegaUsage: Final deliverable assembly, PDF generation, complex merges

presentationGeneration.name: python-pptx
presentationGeneration.bestFor: Converting Python analysis into final decks, automated slide generation
presentationGeneration.omegaUsage: Client presentations, automated reporting decks, chart embedding

selectionMatrix.description: Decision matrix for document generation approach

scenarios.rationale: Full control over formatting, embedded charts
Designer controls branding, Python fills data

usageNotes: Always start with the question: What decision does this chart support?
Choose the simplest chart type that conveys the insight
Test readability at actual presentation size (not zoomed in)
Get feedback from someone unfamiliar with the data
Iterate based on 'So what?' test - can viewer understand in 3 seconds?
Reference this library when generating charts in scripts
Maintain consistency across all charts in a document/presentation
Update chart data sources and dates regularly

withDocx.javascript: Use ImageRun to embed charts as PNG/JPG. Generate charts with Chart.js, export as images.
withDocx.python_programmatic: Use python-docx: Document(), add_heading(), add_paragraph(), add_table(), add_picture()

withExcel.javascript: Use ExcelJS charts API for native Excel charts in workbooks.
withExcel.python_openpyxl: Use openpyxl: Workbook(), create_sheet(), cell styling, openpyxl.chart for native charts
withExcel.python_matplotlib: Generate matplotlib charts, save as PNG, embed with openpyxl.drawing.image.Image()
withExcel.python_pandas: Use df.to_excel() with ExcelWriter for quick data export, then enhance with openpyxl

withPowerPoint.javascript: Use pptxgenjs library to create charts directly in PPTX files.
withPowerPoint.python: Use python-pptx: Presentation(), add_slide(), shapes.add_chart(), shapes.add_picture()

withPDF.from_word: Generate Word with python-docx/docxtpl, convert to PDF with Spire.Doc or LibreOffice
withPDF.direct: Use reportlab for complex layouts, weasyprint for HTML-to-PDF, fpdf2 for simple PDFs

withDashboards.interactive: Use Plotly: fig = px.bar(), fig.write_html() for self-contained interactive HTML
withDashboards.embedding: Plotly charts can be embedded in Jupyter notebooks or exported as static images
